title: Zipper pagination with hierarchical index hinting for low-tail dashboard queries
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Background: Several customers and internal dashboards observe high tail latencies (P95-P99) when running exploratory time-series queries that page across large, multi-tenant result sets. Current cursor-forward pagination often forces wide scans and repeated index hops for adjacent pages, which amplifies I/O and increases variance for tenants with uneven event distributions.

Problem statement: Reduce tail latency for paginated dashboard queries (esp. exploratory workflows like 'find top sessions then drill into events') without regressing average latency or increasing token/compute costs. Relevant symptoms: spikes in P99 when queries cross shard boundaries or when many small time buckets cause index fanout.

Goals / success metrics:
- Reduce P99 single-page fetch latency from ~620ms to <250ms for common query shapes (tenant-scoped time-window with top-k aggregation).
- Reduce P99 for multi-page exploration (3 consecutive pages) from ~1.4s to <400ms.
- No more than 5% increase in total read amplification (unit-cost) at median.

Proposal summary: Implement a zipper-pagination mode combined with hierarchical index hinting and a lightweight predictive prefix cache.
- Zipper pagination: instead of strictly forward cursors, interleave page ranges by fetching anchored windows (centered slices) and stitch results client-side to present contiguous pages. This reduces the number of independent index seeks when users request nearby pages. Zipper mode will be opt-in per-route and fall back to standard cursor pagination.
- Hierarchical index hints: accept optional hint metadata (tenant_id, route_group, primary-time-bucket) from the Console client so the query planner can preferentially use the narrowest shard index and avoid wide fanout. Hints are advisory; planner will validate and ignore if inconsistent.
- Predictive prefix/KV cache: maintain a small LRU cache of top prefixes (tenant+route+recent-buckets) and pre-warm KV lookups for the next likely page during page render. The cache will be size-limited (configurable) and decay keys by recency and weight to avoid cold-object pollution.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Zipper mode increases temporary read parallelism for anchored windows but reduces duplicate seeks across pages — good for tail latency but can raise median reads for single page. We limit aggressive anchoring to queries with estimated cardinality > X (heuristic) to avoid overhead on cheap queries.
- Hierarchical hints require client changes in Console; we will add best-effort generation in the Console SDK and a server-side fallback when hints are absent. Hints are not trusted for correctness.
- Predictive prefix caching trades memory for fewer remote index calls. We will start with a conservative default cache size (64k keys) and measure.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Spike (1 week): prototype zipper stitcher in dashboard API layer and a planner hook that accepts hierarchical hint fields. Create a synthetic workload locally to measure P50/P99 improvement.
2) Engine changes (2 weeks): add zipper fetch paths in query executor, implement anchor selection heuristic, and add opt-in flag in route configs.
3) Cache layer (1 week): implement a small in-process LRU for prefix/KV prefetch, expose runtime knobs (cache size, prefetch window).
4) Console integration (1 week parallel): add hint emission in client SDK for routes that have structured metadata; roll out as opt-in in Canary.
5) Canary rollout (2 weeks): enable zipper mode and cache for 5% of traffic on internal dashboards and two low-risk customers, collect telemetry, and iterate.
6) Ramp and guardrails (1 week): add circuit-breakers and metrics-based automatic disabling if read amplification or error rate increases beyond thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bench harness shows P99 single-page <250ms and 3-page <400ms for target queries on canary tenants.
- No more than 7% increase in median read ops and <10% cost variance across canary.
- Automated tests for zipper stitcher correctness (ordering invariant + dedupe) and planner hint validation.
- Feature flagging and per-tenant kill switch implemented.

Observability and measurement:
- Add new telemetry tags: pagination_mode=zipper|cursor, hint_used=true|false, anchor_distance, prefetch_hit=true|false.
- Dashboards: P50/P95/P99 by tenant tier and pagination_mode, read amplification ratio, cache hit rate, and error/retry counts.
- Perf test: compare against baseline using existing load generator (see runbook link below).

Rollout/runbook links:
- Design doc (internal): https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/console-zipper-pagination-design (placeholder)
- GH spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2314 (will be added)
- Load dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/console-pagination/perf-baseline

Risks & mitigation:
- Incorrect hinting could lead planner to suboptimal indexes — mitigate by conservative validation and telemetry-driven flagging.
- Memory pressure from prefix cache — start small and expose limits; evict aggressively.
- Increased client complexity — keep Console SDK changes minimal and backward compatible; server handles missing hints.

Notes for reviewers:
- Evaluate the anchor selection heuristic in the spike; we should prefer anchors that minimize crossing of shard boundaries and have stable TTL.
- Consider integration with KV cache TTL tuning already discussed in ENG-30482.
comments: 2026-02-23 - Spike started. Built a basic zipper stitcher that merges three anchored windows. Local synthetic test shows 35% P99 improvement for multi-page workloads but 8% extra reads for single-page cases.
2026-02-27 - Design review with PM & Console team. PM requested per-route opt-in and telemetry tags. Console team will add hint exposure in SDK; we agreed it will be best-effort and opt-in.

2026-03-03 - Implementation of anchor heuristic in progress. Initial heuristic uses median time-bucket within requested window and tenant cardinality estimate from route stats. Added unit tests for ordering/dedupe.
2026-03-05 - Feedback from infra: ensure prefix cache is bounded and uses tenant-scoped quota to avoid noisy-tenant eviction blast. We'll add tenant budget hooks in phase 3.

2026-03-09 - Canary plan approved. Targets: enable on internal-apps (10%) then external canary (5%). Monitoring playbook prepared. Linking GH branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/compare/zipper-pagination (draft)

2026-03-10 - Blocker discovered: a rare race when stitching pages with concurrent invalidation of KV prefixes. Mitigation: use generation tokens on cache entries; short-term disable prefetch for routes with high write churn. Added ticket ENG-80034 to address generation tokens.
